title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.23344v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. translated_title: 语言模型学会改进语言模型
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正被越来越多地用于自动化AI研究，包括语言模型（LM）本身的开发，这为递归自我改进提供了一条潜在路径。然而，将实验反馈转化为一种可学习的、能够跨模型提出有效改进的能力面临两大挑战。首先，使用真实反馈来训练这种能力代价高昂：强化学习（RL）需要评估数以万计的改进提案，而每个提案可能都需要一次完整的模型训练运行。即使每次运行仅需十个GPU小时，仅奖励收集这一项就会消耗数十万GPU小时，这促使人们寻求更便宜的替代反馈。其次，当提案分布发生偏移时，替代反馈可能变得不可靠，因为策略优化会偏向那些被高估的提案。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了LM2LM，该方法通过强化学习训练LLM来生成有效的LM改进提案。为了提供可扩展的反馈，我们使用了一种……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出LM2LM方法，通过强化学习训练大语言模型生成有效的语言模型改进提案，并利用廉价的代理反馈解决真实训练反馈成本高昂以及分布偏移下反馈不可靠这两大难题，为递归自我改进铺路。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes LM2LM, which uses reinforcement learning to train LLMs to generate effective language model improvement proposals, leveraging cheap surrogate feedback to overcome the prohibitive cost of real training feedback and its unreliability under proposal distribution shift.
